info.cls_ename: Bachelor's Program of International Business Administration in English

description.describe_ch:
本課程將分析歐洲和國際經濟在當代的演變過程。以此角度探討從工業革命到全球化對經濟體系結構方面的變化，並關注世界重要經濟體的社會和經濟政策，討論現代工業社會的誕生，及數位和資訊科技所引發對經濟和社會影響。
並關注全球化、人口變遷、數位革命、經濟的生態轉換、經濟不平等、金融危機等重要經濟議題。將依主題研究經濟成長、市場變化、科學技術創新、工業革命本質、金融與貨幣體系、國際貿易。
description.describe_eh:
The course will analyze the evolutionary processes of the European and International economy in the modern and contemporary age. 
In this perspective, will be studied the structural aspects of the economic system that led to industrialization and its evolution (from the industrial revolution to the recent transformations produced by globalization), with attention to the social aspects and economic policies of the major world economic areas.
The course will focus on a comparative analysis of two great transformations that occurred in the contemporary age, the first industrial revolution and the birth of modern industrial society and the technological revolution triggered by the advent of digital and computer-based technologies and their economic and social consequences.
Some crucial themes to today's economic will be the subject of debate: globalization; demographic change; the digital revolution; the ecological conversion of the economy; economic inequality; financial crises.
The course will then examine, by topics, economic growth by considering the emergence of markets, scientific knowledge and technological innovations, the nature of the industrial revolutions, financial and monetary systems, international trade.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new_en:
In class participation – Full attendance is expected. While being in class students are required a proactive attitude
Students presentation – Students will be ask, in group or individually, to do exercises and presentations on assigned topics.
Assessment of students learning through the use of multiple choice tests – The Midterm examination consists of the assessment test will cover the contents of the all the lessons taught until the week before the test.
Final presentation, in group or individual – The final presentation consists of a mixed test using multiple choice tests and open questions or reports on the topics covered in class.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Expected classroom behavior
Students should attend class on time.
During lessons it is not possible to use cell phones, IPads or PCs except for taking notes.
All students are expected to treat everyone with respect in the classroom and to behave reasonably, responsibly, and courteously at all times.
Students listen attentively when classmates present or ask questions. When you present, you should speak loud enough to your group or class so that they can hear you clearly.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en:
Diversity and Inclusion
All course activities will be carried out in an atmosphere of friendly participation and interaction among students, respecting and appreciating each student’s personal experience, background and perspectives, such as various school system at home and abroad, diverse enrollment and learning cultures, gender, etc.
You are expected to apply the highest academic standards throughout this course and to treat fellow students with dignity and respect.
It will be important to create moments of exchange and constructive relationships between students with the aim of improving the comparison and learning of the course contents.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
This course is a BIBA course, students must invest the time necessary to be properly prepared for class.
Students are required to participate in team discussion and team assignment.
Copying texts without properly citing the source is not permitted. Plagiarism is a serious breach of academic trust.
For example, it is considered cheating if you copy someone else's answers during an assessment, or if you turn in a paper or assignment that was written in whole or in part by someone else when you turned in an assignment.
